paragraphs: Friend, a list of thirty-one kings is not the most exciting reading, and I say that as a stamper who once got excited about a new rubber band. But look at how careful the writer is. Every king gets his own line, and every line ends with the same word: "one" (Joshua 12:9-24). Nobody gets tossed in with "and a few other fellows," and the list closes with "thirty-one kings in all" (Joshua 12:24).

Notice who is on this record, too. Moses, the servant of the LORD, and the Israelites struck down the kings on the east side, and Joshua and the Israelites conquered the kings on the west (Joshua 12:6-7). Different leaders, same careful record. And the land didn't stay with the leaders. Moses gave the eastern land as an inheritance to the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh, and Joshua gave the western land as an inheritance to the tribes of Israel (Joshua 12:6-7).

So here's my big idea, baker. This record doesn't stop at kings counted. It lands on land handed out as an inheritance, a place for each tribe to call its own (Joshua 12:6-7). I think that's a good word for the days you feel like one more line on a list nobody scrolls, because the people on this list were given something. When you're counting up your days, friend, count what's been handed to you too.
